solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ladder, second missed? Here's horrid old snake

indicators.note: the letter in second place of the word is missed out, dropped from it

parts.note: a stepladder, or a flight of steps

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a ladder rung was skipped, then points out a nasty old snake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like S, the usual abbreviation, but here it means the second letter, T.
explanation.definitionFit: The seps is a venomous serpent of classical legend, now an archaic word, so a horrid old snake.

clue.text: Sewer, a mess when it's burst, to soak up

indicators.note: something burst is broken apart, so its letters scatter into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up reads the word from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to ret flax is to soak it to soften the fibres

explanation.surface: A burst sewer pipe makes a mess and soaks everything around it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sewer' is read as a drain, but it is one who sews (rhyming with 'grower').
explanation.definitionFit: A seamster is a person who stitches clothes for a living, an old word for a tailor.

clue.text: Small number after soft or hard stuff?

parts.note: p for piano, the musical direction meaning soft
taken as written
no. is the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: A tot of something after soft drinks or spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard stuff' suggests spirits, but the question mark points to hardcore material; 'after' places the number at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Pornography at its most explicit is called hardcore, so porno can be cheekily described as hard stuff.

clue.text: Old bucket, mostly bent

indicators.note: mostly means not all of it, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: stooped means bent over

explanation.surface: An antique pail that has become largely dented and misshapen.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoope is an obsolete spelling of stoup, a pail or vessel for liquid, hence an old bucket.

clue.text: Yard in Glossop converted for cottonseed extract

indicators.note: something converted is changed into another form, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: y is the abbreviation for yard
Glossop is a town in Derbyshire, taken as written

explanation.surface: A yard in the Derbyshire town is turned over to processing cotton seeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' just puts the Y among the town's letters before the whole lot is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Gossypol is a toxic yellow pigment obtained from the seeds of the cotton plant.

clue.text: Riotous rag before degree? One probably avoided that

indicators.note: riotous means wild and disorderly, so the letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
D is the abbreviation for degree

explanation.surface: A wild student rag before graduation, which a studious type probably stayed away from.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition refers back to the riotous rag: a student rag is a charity stunt, and a diligent graduate probably kept clear of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A grad, short for graduate, is someone who earned a degree, presumably by skipping the riotous student stunts.

clue.text: One that's ambitious furled spritsail

indicators.note: a furled sail is rolled up and folded, so its letters are twisted into a new arrangement

parts.note: a sail spread by a sprit, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An ambitious sailor rolls up the spritsail.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiralist is a careerist who climbs upward by moving from job to job, so an ambitious person.

clue.text: Rock king replaced by name in field of activity

indicators.note: replaced by tells us one letter is taken out and another put in its place

parts.note: a sphere is one's domain or area of activity
R for rex, Latin for king
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A king of rock music is replaced by a big name in his field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' suggests music, but it is the definition in its geological sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Sphene is the mineral titanite, a calcium titanium silicate found in rocks.

clue.text: Upmarket retirement association favouring public transport

parts.note: pro means in favour of
a bus is public transport

explanation.surface: A posh club for retired people prefers to travel by bus.
explanation.walkthrough: Probus is a club, widespread in Britain and Australia, for retired professional and business people.
explanation.definitionFit: Probus clubs gather retired professionals, so it is an association for the retired with a smart membership.

clue.text: Surviving excursion with cargo on board

indicators.note: with ... on board means carrying something inside, so one word is put inside another

parts.note: an outing is a trip or excursion
a last is an old measure of cargo or load

explanation.surface: A boat trip survives despite the vessel carrying a load.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last' as a unit of cargo is an old measure of weight for a ship's load.
explanation.definitionFit: Outlasting means living longer than or enduring beyond something, which is surviving it.

clue.text: Break down 'alternative facts' de nos jours, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the word is judged by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: 'alternative facts' was the notorious modern euphemism for falsehoods

explanation.surface: A jibe at the political euphemism for untruths in our times, as said aloud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'De nos jours' (French: of our days) marks 'alternative facts' as the modern phrase for lies.
explanation.definitionFit: To lyse is to cause cells to disintegrate, a biochemical term for breaking down.

clue.text: Cockney's false claim about Victorian murder investigator, a self-aggrandiser?

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker drops the aitch at the start of a word

parts.words: false claim about Victorian murder investigator
parts.note: 'he got Ripper': a false boast about a Victorian detective, since Jack the Ripper was never caught

explanation.surface: A Cockney falsely boasts about a Victorian detective, which sounds like self-promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: The claim 'He got (the) Ripper' is false because the Whitechapel murderer was never identified; the Cockney drops its first H.
explanation.definitionFit: An ego-tripper indulges in vain self-glorifying behaviour, which is what a self-aggrandiser does.

clue.text: Sailor travelling in foreign parts

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
on the road means travelling

explanation.surface: A sailor on the move in other countries.
explanation.definitionFit: Abroad means in or to a foreign country, overseas, away from one's homeland.

clue.text: A minute bit in mixture to prepare as road surface?

indicators.note: a mixture blends things together, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A tiny amount goes into the mix used to lay a road.
explanation.definitionFit: To bituminate is to coat or treat with bitumen, the tarry material used in road surfacing.

clue.text: Reverse of silence, also included loud laughter?

indicators.note: the reverse of something reads it the opposite way round
one word included in another is put inside it

parts.note: sh is a call for silence
too means also

explanation.surface: The opposite of quiet, and loud guffaws were part of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoots are loud bursts of laughter, as in 'hoots of derision'.

clue.text: Aussie footballers score O so freely (about 100)

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the extra letter goes in among the others
freely means without fixed arrangement, so the letters move about

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Australia's football team score with ease, a hundred goals near enough.
explanation.definitionFit: The Socceroos is the nickname of Australia's men's national association football team.

clue.text: Quake, not the first, making Geordie move out?

indicators.note: not the first means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: to quake is to tremble

explanation.surface: A minor earthquake prompts someone from Newcastle to leave home.
explanation.walkthrough: A Geordie is a native of Tyneside in north-east England; remble is northern dialect.
explanation.definitionFit: Remble is a northern English dialect verb meaning to remove or clear away, so a Geordie's word for moving out.

clue.text: South African country admits little positive in hesitant policy

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for south

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the country takes a letter inside it

parts.note: Togo is a country in West Africa
P is short for positive

explanation.surface: A southern African nation allows a little optimism into its wavering policy.
explanation.definitionFit: Stop-go describes an economic policy of alternate restraint and expansion, hence a hesitant one.

clue.text: Pacific island one introduced to eucalyptus

indicators.note: introduced to means brought inside, so a letter goes into the word

parts.note: a gum tree is a eucalyptus
a means one

explanation.surface: A single eucalyptus tree is brought to an island in the Pacific.
explanation.definitionFit: Guam is a US territory in the western Pacific Ocean, the largest of the Mariana Islands.

clue.text: Members of barberry family: chap circling house is holding one

indicators.note: circling means going round, so one word surrounds another

parts.note: a man is a chap
HO is the abbreviation for house

indicators.note: holding means keeping something inside, so a letter is held within

parts.note: taken as written
a means one

explanation.surface: A man walks round a house that contains an example of barberry shrubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahonias are evergreen shrubs, including Oregon grape, belonging to the barberry family Berberidaceae.

clue.text: Having small swellings cut, bleed badly round centre of perforation

indicators.note: badly means not properly, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter alone

parts.note: the sixth of eleven letters

explanation.surface: Lumpy skin, when cut, bleeds heavily around the puncture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' only says the middle letter joins the mix; everything is then rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: Tubercled means covered with tubercles, small rounded nodules or swellings on skin or a plant.

clue.text: Not on the right track? Third taking lead looked pleased

indicators.note: the third letter takes the lead, removed from its place and put in front

parts.note: misled means led astray, set off on the wrong path

explanation.surface: Someone off course takes the lead in third place and beams with pleasure.
explanation.definitionFit: To smile is to show pleasure with the face, so smiled means looked pleased.

clue.text: One seriously disturbed? Coop is wrong in place of hospital

indicators.note: wrong means not right, so the letters are put in a different order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
at means in a place, as in 'at home'
H is the abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A deranged patient is wrongly kept in a cage rather than a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In place of' looks like a substitution signal, but it splits: 'in place' is AT, and 'of' just attaches the hospital abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A sociopath has a severe personality disorder marked by antisocial behaviour, so is seriously disturbed.

clue.text: Tense person departs, say when climbing (6, two words)

parts.note: one means a person, as in 'one never knows'
d is the abbreviation for departs on timetables

indicators.note: climbing in a down entry means reading upwards, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: e.g. means for example, as 'say' does

explanation.surface: A nervous person leaves while ascending, for instance on a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: On edge is an idiom for nervous and irritable, a synonym of tense.

clue.text: Crufts entry maybe turned up good and clean, with grand following (6, two words)

indicators.note: turned means reversed in direction, so the word reads back to front

parts.note: taken as written
G is the abbreviation for good
to do a room is to clean it
G is short for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: A show dog arrives well groomed, with a big prize to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: Crufts is Britain's best-known dog show; 'maybe' marks the answer as one example of an entrant.
explanation.definitionFit: A pug dog is a small snub-nosed breed that could well be entered at a dog show.

clue.text: Heads for refuge in monsoon under conifer

indicators.note: heads are the tops, the first letters of the following words

parts.note: first letters of these four words

explanation.surface: Someone makes for shelter beneath a tree during the monsoon.
explanation.definitionFit: The rimu is a tall New Zealand conifer, also called red pine.

clue.text: Macho man with 'Whoopee!' joined film company

parts.note: a stud is a virile man
io is an old exclamation of joy or triumph

explanation.surface: A hunk gleefully signs up with a movie firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A studio is a company that makes films, as in the Hollywood studios.

clue.text: Laundryman in Frankfurt that is given sash

parts.note: d.h., das heisst, is the German for 'that is'
an obi is a Japanese sash

explanation.surface: A laundry worker in a German city receives a sash.
explanation.definitionFit: A dhobi is a washerman in India, someone who launders clothes for a living.

clue.text: Control's back, seizing power one picks off the unwary

indicators.note: back means turned around, so the word runs in the opposite direction
seizing means grabbing hold, so a letter is taken inside

parts.note: reins are a means of control
P is the abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: Mission control's back-up team seizes power from a gunman targeting the careless.
explanation.definitionFit: A sniper shoots from cover at people who are unaware, picking them off one at a time.

clue.text: Holder of weapon that's slashed bard — here's mark of earlier wound

indicators.note: something slashed has a piece cut away, so the named word is lopped off the end

parts.note: a scabbard is the sheath that holds a sword
the poet's word, the chunk cut from the end

explanation.surface: A sword's sheath was cut through by a poet, leaving a reminder of an old injury.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the last four letters, BARD, from SCABBARD and SCAB remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A scab is the crust that forms over a healing cut, so it marks where a wound once was.

clue.text: Signs of dismissal of old, as 'Push off!'

indicators.note: off means not right or out of order, so the letters are reshuffled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Old-fashioned gestures of contempt, like telling someone to go away.
explanation.definitionFit: Puh is an obsolete interjection expressing contempt, so puhs are old exclamations of dismissal.

clue.text: Warm or cold, requiring a hat

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
taken as written
lid is slang for a hat

explanation.surface: Whether the weather is warm or chilly, you need a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Warm or cold' looks like a pair of opposites to choose between; 'Warm' is the definition and 'cold' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Calid is a rare word, from Latin calidus, meaning warm or hot.

clue.text: After party in prison I'll be seen in sporting get-up

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one word goes within another

parts.note: jug is slang for prison
a do is a party
taken as written

explanation.surface: A prisoner announces what they will wear once the party in jail is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts I after the jailed party.
explanation.definitionFit: A judogi is the white jacket and trousers worn for judo, a sporting outfit.

clue.text: Hating hard work? So pub'll have charm

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore, so
PH is the abbreviation for public house
obia, or obeah, is a fetish or charm used in Caribbean folk magic

explanation.surface: Someone who dodges hard work thinks the pub will be appealing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergophobia is a morbid fear or dislike of work, so it fits the question-marked hatred of toil.

clue.text: Requests doctor replacing hospital for confinements

indicators.note: replacing means one item takes the place of another letter

parts.note: behests are commands or requests
Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
H is the abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A doctor asks that patients be sent somewhere other than hospital to recover.
explanation.definitionFit: Bed rests are periods of confinement to bed, prescribed for recovery or in pregnancy.

clue.text: Hard drinks? Try some oulong instead

indicators.note: some means a portion, so the letters come from inside the following words

parts.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: Someone offered spirits suggests oolong tea as an alternative.
explanation.walkthrough: Oulong is a variant spelling of oolong, a Chinese tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Gins are spirits, strong alcoholic drinks, which are often called hard drinks.
